Well, there are two things wrong with that plan.

  1. If you don't distribute anything, it isn't going to be very useful as a general purpose tool.

  2. Without a central authority there would be no way to stop someone from coming in and stealing your domain.

That said, if this is something you are really looking for, it's definitely possible. Just setup your own DNS server and don't have it do referrals. That's what most folks who want to avoid bans do.

What i am thinking is to drop the whole DNS system as it works today and have something that comes preinstalled with your OS, some kind of always-running service. By connecting to the Internet you agree to become part of the system and you begin "hosting" a part of the Domain Names, in a way similar to how FreeNet works [https://freenetproject.org/documentation.html#content]. Or perhaps a way like bitcoins work with the need to reach a widespread consensus before a domain name is assigned to your IP. In this way no one would be able to steal a domain once granted and it would be a free service with he "cost" shared among the users.

Of course the evil is in the details... for instance, how do you stop someone from registering an "infinite" number of domains? How does a domain change "owner"? How to implement this in a way that it is as fast as current domain name servers (at least for read-only purposes)? They are not easy questions to answer, but perhaps not that hard either.

Btw, i am not trying to solve the problem only for myself, but to have a general solution that makes it impossible, or very very hard, for someone, even a government, to sabotage or control the system.
